name: Build a section's weekly timetable, clash-checked as it is assigned, and publish it once approved
priorityReason: Period attendance, teacher duties and every family's day read the published timetable. Nothing else produces it.

goal.capability: to assign a subject and a teacher to each slot of a section's week and publish it once approved
goal.outcome: every section has a workable week, nobody is booked twice, and no timetable commits a teacher's week without approval

businessRules.rule: A timetable is held against a section, not a class. A class carries several sections, and 5-A and 5-B have different teachers in different slots, which a timetable held against the class cannot express.
A slot is assigned a subject the class carries and a teacher who teaches it. A subject not attached to the class cannot be timetabled for it.
Every assignment is checked for clashes as it is made, and one that conflicts is refused rather than saved and reported later. A clash saved is a clash somebody discovers on the day.
A teacher cannot be assigned where they are already teaching another section in that slot, and a section cannot hold two subjects in the same slot.
A room cannot be booked twice in the same slot where a room is set.
A teacher cannot be assigned where they are already covering as a substitute in that slot, or where they are unavailable — on approved leave or otherwise marked unavailable.
A refusal names what the assignment clashed against. Told only that there is a conflict, a coordinator has to find it themselves.

Whenever an assignment is refused the system also lists the teachers actually free in that slot — those who teach the subject and have no class, no substitute cover and no unavailability at that time — so a replacement is chosen from a list rather than by checking every teacher by hand.
While the timetable is a draft the coordinator builds and edits it freely, and nothing in it is visible to a teacher, a student or a guardian.
A timetable cannot be published unapproved, because it commits every teacher's working week. The Coordinator builds and the School Admin approves.

A change to a published timetable goes back through the same approval, and carries a written reason. A slot moved after families and staff have planned around it is a different act from an edit to a draft.
Once a change is approved, every affected teacher, student and guardian is told exactly what changed — which slot, from what, to what — rather than being told the timetable has been updated.
A published timetable is what period attendance and teacher duties read. A slot that does not exist in it cannot be marked or assigned.
The timetable is built against a period structure — how many periods a day, on which days, at what times. No feature in the document creates one, and it must exist before any timetable can be built.
A timetable is never deleted. A section whose timetable is replaced carries the previous one as superseded, so a past week stays readable.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Loads the section's period structure as an empty grid, held against the section rather than the class.

basicFlow.function: assignSlot(sectionId, day, periodId, subjectId, teacherId, roomId)
basicFlow.systemResponse: Checks the subject is one the class carries and the teacher teaches it.
Checks the teacher against other sections, the section against other subjects, the room against other bookings, the teacher against substitute cover, and the teacher against leave and unavailability.

basicFlow.systemResponse: Saves the slot where nothing clashes, or refuses it and names what it clashed against.

basicFlow.userAction: Builds and edits the draft freely, then submits it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds it at Awaiting approval. Nothing in a draft was ever visible to a teacher, a student or a guardian.

basicFlow.userAction: Reviews the timetable and approves it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records the approval, which is what permits publication.
Publishes it. Each teacher sees their own weekly schedule and each section its own, and period attendance and teacher duties now read it.

basicFlow.userAction: Proposes a change to a published timetable, with a reason, which goes back through the same approval.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Holds the change for the School Admin. On approval every affected teacher, student and guardian is told exactly what changed.

alternateFlows.condition: The room is already booked in that slot

alternateFlows.navigation: Timetable builder → Free teachers in this slot → Assign
alternateFlows.behaviour: They choose from the teachers who teach the subject and are genuinely free, rather than checking every teacher by hand (BR-8).

alternateFlows.condition: The School Admin does not approve
alternateFlows.behaviour: It returns to the Coordinator with a reason. Nothing has been published and nobody has planned around it.

departures.requirement: The five clash checks run as the assignment is made and complete within 500 milliseconds, because a check that runs on save is a check the coordinator works around.
There is no route by which a clashing assignment is persisted, including a bulk import or a generated timetable. The refusal is the control.
The free-teacher list accounts for teaching, cover, leave and marked unavailability together. A list that omits any of the four sends the coordinator to somebody who is not free.
A draft is not sent to a teacher, student or guardian view at all, rather than hidden there.
A change to a published timetable notifies everybody affected before the changed slot arrives.
Timetables and their changes are retained for the academic session and 3 years afterwards, since attendance records reference them.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
